spec.description: A reference dashboard of common LogQL query patterns. Copy any panel and replace the label names/values with your own to get started quickly.

options.content:
## 📖 LogQL Query Templates

This dashboard is a **reference library** of common LogQL query patterns. Each panel demonstrates a specific query technique.

### How to copy a template
1. Click the panel menu (⋮) → **Edit**
2. Copy the query from the query editor
3. Paste into your own dashboard or Explore
4. Replace placeholders like `your-app-name` and `your-namespace` with your actual label names and values

| Section | What's covered |
|---|---|
| **Basic Queries** | Stream selectors, label matchers |
| **Line Filters** | `\|=` contains, `!=` exclude, `\|~` regex |
| **Parsing** | JSON, logfmt, pattern, regexp extraction |
| **Metrics from Logs** | `rate()`, `count_over_time()`, `bytes_rate()` |
| **Aggregations** | `unwrap`, `quantile_over_time`, `avg_over_time` |

> 💡 **Tip:** Use **Explore** (compass icon in the left sidebar) to test and refine queries before adding them to a dashboard.

spec.title: String: ToLower / ToUpper / title
spec.description:
ToLower/ToUpper convert case. title capitalizes each word. lower/upper are aliases.

🔧 Customize:
• ToLower .level → "ERROR" becomes "error"
• ToUpper .method → "get" becomes "GET"
• title .status → "not found" becomes "Not Found"
• Use in label_format too: | label_format level="{{ ToLower .level }}"
• swapcase .str → inverts the case of every character

spec.title: String: Trim / TrimPrefix / TrimSuffix / trimAll
spec.description:
TrimSpace removes leading/trailing whitespace. TrimPrefix/TrimSuffix remove a specific affix. trimAll removes any of the specified characters from both ends. nospace removes ALL spaces.

🔧 Customize:
• TrimSpace .message → removes \n, \t, spaces from edges
• TrimPrefix .path "/api/v1" → strips the prefix
• TrimSuffix .filename ".log" → strips the suffix
• trimAll "!? " .message → removes any of those chars from both ends
• nospace .tag → removes every space in the string

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | json | line_format `msg={{ TrimSpace .message }} path={{ TrimPrefix .path "/api/v1" }} file={{ TrimSuffix .filename ".log" }}`

spec.title: String: Replace / regexReplaceAll
spec.description:
Replace substitutes a substring N times (-1 = all). regexReplaceAll uses a RE2 regex with optional capture group back-references ($1, $2) in the replacement. regexReplaceAllLiteral treats the replacement literally (no back-references).

🔧 Customize:
• Replace .str "old" "new" -1 → all occurrences
• Replace .str "old" "new" 1 → first occurrence only
• regexReplaceAll "pattern" .field "replacement"
• Use $1 in replacement to reference capture group 1
• Great for redacting PII: IPs, emails, card numbers

spec.title: String: Contains / HasPrefix / regexFind
spec.description:
Contains/HasPrefix/HasSuffix return boolean for use in conditionals. regexFind returns the first regex match. regexFindAll returns all matches as a list. regexMatch returns true/false.

🔧 Customize:
• Contains .path "/api" → true if path includes /api
• HasPrefix .path "/api/v1" → true if starts with /api/v1
• regexFind "\\d+" .message → first number in message
• regexMatch "error" .level → true/false match
• Combine with if: {{ if Contains .path "/admin" }}ADMIN{{ end }}

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | json | line_format `api={{ Contains .path "/api" }} v1={{ HasPrefix .path "/api/v1" }} id={{ regexFind "\\d+" .path }}`

spec.title: String: splitList / join / trunc / substr
spec.description:
splitList splits a string into a list by a delimiter. join concatenates a list back. trunc truncates to N chars. substr extracts by index. repeat repeats a string N times.

🔧 Customize:
• splitList "." .hostname → ["host","domain","com"]
• first / last / rest work on the list result
• trunc 20 .message → first 20 characters (add "..." manually)
• substr 0 10 .message → characters at index 0-9
• join (splitList "/" .path) "-" → replace / with -

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | json | line_format `host={{ first (splitList "." .hostname) }} short={{ trunc 30 .message }}... parts={{ join (splitList "/" .path) "-" }}`

spec.title: Math: toInt / toFloat64 / toString / toBool
spec.description:
Type conversion functions are required before arithmetic. toInt/toFloat64 convert strings to numbers. toString converts back. toBool parses boolean strings. int64 handles large integers.

🔧 Customize:
• toInt .status_code → "200" → 200
• toFloat64 .duration_ms → "1.5" → 1.5
• toString .request_count → 123 → "123"
• toBool .enabled → "true" → true
• atoi is an alias for toInt
• int64 handles values that overflow int (>2^31)

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | logfmt | line_format `int={{ toInt .status_code }} float={{ toFloat64 .duration_ms }} str={{ toString .request_count }} bool={{ toBool .enabled }}`

spec.title: Math: add / sub / mul / div / mod
spec.description:
add/sub/mul/div perform integer arithmetic. mod returns the remainder. Note: div truncates to integer. Use divf for float division.

🔧 Customize:
• add (toInt .success_count) (toInt .error_count) → sum
• add takes multiple args: add 1 2 3 → 6
• div (toInt .bytes) 1024 → KB (integer, truncates)
• mod (toInt .request_id) 100 → 0-99 bucket
• Always wrap string fields with toInt before arithmetic

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | logfmt | line_format `total={{ add (toInt .success_count) (toInt .error_count) }} half={{ div (toInt .total_count) 2 }} bucket={{ mod (toInt .request_id) 100 }}`

spec.title: Math: addf / subf / mulf / divf (float)
spec.description:
addf/subf/mulf/divf are the float-aware equivalents of the integer functions. Always use toFloat64 to convert string fields first. Combine with printf to control decimal places.

🔧 Customize:
• divf (toFloat64 .duration_ms) 1000.0 → seconds as float
• mulf (toFloat64 .ratio) 100.0 → percentage (0-1 → 0-100)
• subf (toFloat64 .end_time) (toFloat64 .start_time) → elapsed
• Pipe to printf: divf .ms 1000.0 | printf "%.2f"
• For mixed int/float: addf (toFloat64 (toInt .int_field)) .float_field

spec.title: Math: ceil / floor / round / max / min
spec.description:
ceil rounds up to next integer. floor rounds down. round rounds to N decimal places. max/min return the larger/smaller of two values.

🔧 Customize:
• ceil (divf .bytes 1024.0) → always round UP to next KB
• floor (divf .bytes 1048576.0) → round DOWN to MB
• round value 2 → round to 2 decimal places
• min 5000 (toInt .duration_ms) → cap at 5000ms
• max 0 (toInt .delta) → clamp negative values to 0

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | logfmt | line_format `ceil={{ ceil (divf (toFloat64 .bytes) 1024.0) }}KB floor={{ floor (divf (toFloat64 .bytes) 1048576.0) }}MB clamped={{ min 9999 (max 0 (toInt .duration_ms)) }}ms`

spec.title: Date: now / unixEpoch
spec.description:
now returns the current time as time.Time. unixEpoch converts time.Time to Unix epoch seconds (integer). Use with toDate to convert log timestamp strings.

🔧 Customize:
• unixEpoch now → current Unix timestamp as integer
• unixEpoch (toDate "layout" .field) → log timestamp as Unix seconds
• Common Go layout: "2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00" (RFC3339)
• For milliseconds: mul (unixEpoch (toDate "..." .ts)) 1000
• Note: Go uses a fixed reference time (Jan 2 15:04:05 2006) for format strings

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | json | line_format `log_unix={{ unixEpoch (toDate "2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00" .timestamp) }} now_unix={{ unixEpoch now }}`

spec.title: Date: date / dateInZone / htmlDate
spec.description:
date formats a time.Time using Go's reference time layout. dateInZone does the same but converts to a specified IANA timezone first.

🔧 Customize:
• Go reference time: Mon Jan 2 15:04:05 MST 2006
• Date only: "2006-01-02"
• Time only: "15:04:05"
• Custom: "Jan 2 at 3:04PM"
• dateInZone layout (toDate inputLayout .field) "America/New_York"
• htmlDate uses "2006-01-02" automatically
• htmlDateInZone adds timezone conversion to htmlDate

spec.title: Date: toDate / toDateInTimezone
spec.description:
toDate parses a string timestamp into a time.Time using a Go format layout. toDateInTimezone parses and immediately converts to the specified timezone.

🔧 Customize:
• toDate "format" .field → parse string to time.Time
• Common formats:
  - RFC3339: "2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00"
  - Simple: "2006-01-02T15:04:05"
  - Apache: "02/Jan/2006:15:04:05 -0700"
  - Unix date: "Mon Jan _2 15:04:05 MST 2006"
• toDateInTimezone parses + converts to a named timezone
• Always chain with date/ago/unixEpoch to output the result

spec.title: Date: ago / duration / durationRound
spec.description:
ago returns a human-readable duration since a past time.Time. duration parses a duration string or nanosecond int into time.Duration. durationRound rounds to the largest single unit.

🔧 Customize:
• ago (toDate "..." .timestamp) → "5 minutes ago" / "3 hours ago"
• duration "1.5h" → 1h30m0s
• duration .elapsed_ns → if field is a nanosecond count (integer)
• durationRound (duration .elapsed_ns) → "3h" not "3h4m52s"
• dateModify "+1h" (toDate "..." .ts) → adds 1h to a parsed time

spec.title: Encoding: b64enc / b64dec / b32enc / b32dec
spec.description:
b64enc/b64dec encode and decode Base64 strings. b32enc/b32dec do the same for Base32. Useful for decoding encoded payloads, tokens, or metadata logged as Base64 strings.

🔧 Customize:
• b64dec .encoded_token → decode a Base64 encoded field
• b64enc .plaintext → encode a plain string to Base64
• b32enc/b32dec work the same but use Base32 alphabet
• Common use: decode JWT header/payload fields stored in logs
• Combine: b64dec (regexFind "[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+" .token)

spec.title: Encoding: urlencode / urldecode / urlParse
spec.description:
urlencode percent-encodes a string. urldecode reverses it. urlParse parses a full URL into a struct with accessible fields.

🔧 Customize:
• urldecode .query_string → "%20" becomes " "
• urlencode .value → encodes for use in a URL
• (urlParse .request_url).Host → extract hostname
• (urlParse .request_url).Path → extract path only
• (urlParse .request_url).RawQuery → extract query string
• (urlParse .request_url).Scheme → http or https

spec.title: Encoding: sha256sum / sha1sum / adler32sum
spec.description:
sha256sum/sha1sum/adler32sum compute hashes of a string. Useful for anonymising PII (user IDs, emails, IPs) while preserving uniqueness for correlation.

🔧 Customize:
• sha256sum .user_id → 64-character hex string
• trunc 8 (sha256sum .user_id) → short 8-char identifier
• sha1sum .session_token → 40-character hex hash
• adler32sum is faster but weaker (non-security use only)
• All three take a string input — wrap numbers with toString first

spec.title: Conditional: default
spec.description:
default returns the fallback value when the field is empty (empty string, zero, nil). Essential for handling optional fields after json/logfmt parsing.

🔧 Customize:
• default "info" .level → use "info" if .level is missing
• default "production" .environment
• default "anonymous" .user_id
• Works with numbers too: default 0 .count
• Useful in label_format: | label_format env="{{ default \"prod\" .env }}"
• Triggers on: empty string, 0, nil, false

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | json | line_format `level={{ default "info" .level }} env={{ default "production" .environment }} user={{ default "anonymous" .user_id }}`

spec.title: Conditional: coalesce
spec.description:
coalesce returns the first non-empty value from a list of arguments. More powerful than default when multiple fields might contain the value you need.

🔧 Customize:
• coalesce .user_id .username .sub "anonymous"
• Different services may use different field names for the same concept
• Handles: nil, empty string, zero, false
• Preferred over nested default calls
• coalesce .trace_id .request_id .correlation_id "none"

spec.title: Conditional: ternary
spec.description:
ternary returns value_if_true when the condition is truthy, value_if_false otherwise. Syntax: ternary "true_val" "false_val" condition.

🔧 Customize:
• ternary "🔴 ERROR" "✅ OK" (gt (toInt .status_code) 399)
• ternary "slow" "fast" (gt (toInt .duration_ms) 1000)
• Common predicates: eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge
• Note argument ORDER: ternary true_value false_value condition
• For multi-branch logic, use if/else instead

spec.title: Conditional: if / else if / else / and / or
spec.description:
Full Go template conditionals inside line_format. if/else if/else/end for branching. and/or/not for logical operators. with checks non-empty.

🔧 Customize:
• if / else if / else / end for multi-branch logic
• and (gt .val 0) (lt .val 100) → boolean AND
• or (eq .level "error") (eq .level "fatal") → boolean OR
• not (eq .level "debug") → boolean NOT
• with .user_id → skips block if .user_id is empty; inside, "." is .user_id
• Variables: {{ $class := "error" }} then {{ $class }}

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | json | line_format `{{ if gt (toInt .status_code) 499 }}🔴 5xx{{ else if gt (toInt .status_code) 399 }}🟡 4xx{{ else }}🟢 2xx{{ end }} {{ .method }} {{ .path }}`

spec.title: label_format: Rename Labels
spec.description:
label_format renames existing labels. Left side = new name, right side = old name (as a quoted string).

🔧 Customize:
• | label_format new_name="old_name"
• Comma-separate multiple renames in one stage
• The original label name is removed and replaced with the new name
• Use before line_format so renamed labels are available with the new name
• Reduces cardinality when normalising across services with different field names

spec.title: label_format: Computed Labels from Templates
spec.description:
label_format can create computed labels from Go template expressions. The new label becomes available for use in downstream queries and panel grouping.

🔧 Customize:
• New labels created here become groupable in rate()/sum by() queries
• Great for creating categorical labels from numeric fields
• status_class enables: sum by(status_class) (rate(...))
• latency_bucket enables: sum by(latency_bucket) (count_over_time(...))
• Labels must be valid Prometheus label names (alphanumeric + _)

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | json | label_format status_class=`{{ if lt (toInt .status_code) 400 }}success{{ else if lt (toInt .status_code) 500 }}client_error{{ else }}server_error{{ end }}`, latency_bucket=`{{ if lt (toInt .duration_ms) 100 }}fast{{ else if lt (toInt .duration_ms) 1000 }}normal{{ else }}slow{{ end }}`

spec.title: label_format: Normalise with String Functions
spec.description:
Combine label_format with template string functions to normalise label values for consistency across services with different conventions.

🔧 Customize:
• ToLower .level → "ERROR" → "error" (normalise severity)
• ToUpper .method → "get" → "GET" (normalise HTTP method)
• Replace .service "-" "_" -1 → make label valid for Prometheus
• trunc 50 .message → prevent high cardinality from long strings
• regexReplaceAll "/[0-9]+" .path "/ID" → normalise REST paths

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | json | label_format level=`{{ ToLower .level }}`, method=`{{ ToUpper .method }}`, service=`{{ Replace .app "-" "_" -1 }}`

spec.title: printf: Format Numbers and Strings
spec.description:
printf uses C-style format verbs to control number formatting. Essential for controlling decimal places and adding units to numeric log fields.

🔧 Customize:
• %.2f → 2 decimal places
• %d → integer
• %s → string
• %05d → zero-padded to 5 digits
• %x → lowercase hexadecimal
• %X → uppercase hexadecimal
• Pipe style also works: toFloat64 .ms | printf "%.3f"
• Multiple args: printf "%s took %.2fms" .method (toFloat64 .duration)

spec.title: printf: toHex / toOctal / toBinary / toDecimal
spec.description:
toHex/toOctal/toBinary convert integers to different number bases. toDecimal converts a string number in another base back to decimal. Useful for bitmasks, file modes, error codes.

🔧 Customize:
• toHex (toInt .error_code) → "1a2b" (hex, no 0x prefix)
• toOctal (toInt .file_mode) → "755" (octal permissions)
• toBinary (toInt .flags) → "1010" (binary bitmask inspection)
• toDecimal "ff" → 255 (hex string to decimal int)
• All take an integer. Use toInt first if field is a string.

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | json | line_format `code={{ toInt .status_code }} hex=0x{{ toHex (toInt .error_code) }} oct=0{{ toOctal (toInt .file_mode) }} bits={{ toBinary (toInt .flags) }}`

spec.title: JSON Parsing + Field Filter
spec.description:
Parse structured JSON logs and filter on extracted fields. Works when each log line is a JSON object.

🔧 Customize:
• | json extracts all top-level keys as labels
• Filter extracted fields: | level="error"
• Access nested fields: | json field="outer.inner"
• Rename on parse: | json status="http_status_code"
• Numeric filter: | response_time > 1000

spec.title: logfmt Parsing + Duration Filter
spec.description:
Parse key=value formatted logs (common in Go services). Filter on numeric fields with comparisons.

🔧 Customize:
• logfmt parses key=value pairs
• Duration fields support units: > 1s, > 500ms, > 2m
• Combine filters: | level="error" | duration > 500ms
• Filter strings: | method="GET"
• Works with Go standard library logger format

spec.title: Pattern Extraction
spec.description:
Extract specific fields by matching a fixed-format log structure. Simpler than regex for structured logs.

🔧 Customize:
• <_> skips a field you don't need
• <label_name> captures into a named label
• Adjust the template to match your log format exactly
• Example log: 2024-01-01 level=error msg="connection refused"
• After extraction: | level="error" to filter

spec.title: Regexp Label Extraction
spec.description:
Use RE2 named capture groups to extract labels from unstructured log lines.

🔧 Customize:
• (?P<name>pattern) creates a label called 'name'
• Capture multiple fields in one expression
• Example: "(?P<level>\\w+)\\s+(?P<status>\\d{3})"
• Filter extracted labels after: | level="error"
• Use for non-standard log formats where pattern/json/logfmt won't work

spec.title: Multi-Stage Pipeline (parse → filter → reformat)
spec.description:
Chain parse → filter → reformat in one pipeline. The most powerful LogQL pattern.

🔧 Customize:
• | json or | logfmt first to extract fields
• Filter with label comparisons and line filters
• | line_format rewrites the displayed line using Go template syntax
• {{.label_name}} references an extracted label
• Great for cleaning up noisy log formats for readability

spec.expr: {app="your-app-name"} | json | level=~"error|warn" | status_code >= 400 | line_format "[{{.level}}] status={{.status_code}} msg={{.message}}"

spec.title: Basic Stream Selection
spec.description:
The foundation of every LogQL query. Select log streams using label matchers inside {}.

🔧 Customize:
• Replace 'app' and 'namespace' with your actual label names
• Replace values with your service name and namespace
• Add more labels to narrow the scope: {app="x", env="prod", region="us-east"}

spec.title: Label Regex Matching
spec.description:
Use =~ for regex matching on label values. Useful for selecting multiple services at once.

🔧 Customize:
• =~ matches a regex pattern (RE2 syntax)
• !~ excludes matching label values
• Example: app=~"api-.*" matches any app starting with 'api-'
• Combine: {app=~"svc-a|svc-b", env="prod"}

spec.title: Line Filter — Contains String
spec.description:
Filter log lines to only those containing a specific string. Case-sensitive.

🔧 Customize:
• Replace 'search term' with the string you want to find
• Chain multiple filters: |= "error" |= "database"
• For case-insensitive: use regex instead → |~ "(?i)search term"
• Opposite (exclude): != "unwanted string"

spec.title: Line Filter — Exclude + Regex
spec.description:
Combine exclusion filters and regex to find what you want. Filters chain left-to-right.

🔧 Customize:
• != excludes lines containing the string
• |~ "error|warn|fatal" matches any of the alternatives
• !~ excludes regex matches
• Chain: |= "error" != "expected error" != "test error"

spec.title: Log Volume Rate (lines/sec by app)
spec.description:
Log lines per second, grouped by app. The fundamental volume metric from logs.

🔧 Customize:
• Replace 'your-namespace' with your namespace label value
• Change 'app' in sum by() to group by a different label
• $__auto adjusts the range to match the dashboard time range
• Add filters before [$__auto]: |= "error" to count only error lines
• Unit: set to 'logs/s' or 'short'

spec.title: Error Log Rate (by app)
spec.description:
Rate of error-level log lines, broken down by service. Parse first to get the level label.

🔧 Customize:
• Replace json with logfmt if your logs use key=value format
• Adjust level=~"error|warn" to match your severity values
• Change the sum by(app) label to group differently
• Compare against total rate to get error percentage
• Unit: set to 'logs/s' or 'short'

spec.title: Error Ratio (errors ÷ total)
spec.description:
Fraction of log lines that are errors. Query A = errors, B = total, C = ratio.

🔧 Customize:
• Set panel unit to 'percentunit' (displays 0–1 as 0–100%)
• Match the filter in query A to your error definition
• Query C is a Math expression: $A / $B
• Add thresholds: warn at 0.01 (1%), critical at 0.05 (5%)
• Use stat panel type for a single current-value KPI

spec.title: Top 5 Noisiest Apps (log volume)
spec.description:
Find the top N noisiest services in a namespace by log volume.

🔧 Customize:
• Change 5 to any N (top 3, top 10, etc.)
• Replace 'your-namespace' with your namespace
• Change 'app' in by(app) to group by a different label
• Add a line filter to limit to specific log types
• Great for identifying unexpectedly chatty services

spec.title: count_over_time by Log Level
spec.description:
Count of log lines per time bucket, grouped by an extracted label. Use for trend analysis over a time range.

🔧 Customize:
• sum by(level) groups the count by severity level
• Change 'level' to any extracted label (status_code, method, region)
• Unlike rate(), returns raw counts per interval (not per-second)
• $__auto adapts bucket size to the selected time range
• Useful for building log event histograms

spec.title: unwrap — Avg Duration from Logs
spec.description:
Extract a numeric value from parsed logs and compute the average over each time bucket.

🔧 Customize:
• | logfmt or | json to parse the numeric field first
• | unwrap <field_name> extracts the numeric label
• Supports duration suffixes automatically (e.g. 1.5s, 200ms)
• Also works with: sum_over_time(), min_over_time(), max_over_time(), last_over_time()
• Set unit to 'seconds' or 'milliseconds' to match your values

spec.title: quantile_over_time — p95 Latency from Logs
spec.description:
Calculate percentile latency from a numeric field embedded in logs.

🔧 Customize:
• Change 0.95 to 0.5 (p50), 0.99 (p99), etc.
• Replace 'response_time_ms' with your extracted numeric field name
• Use | json or | logfmt before unwrap to extract the field
• by(app) groups percentiles per service — change or remove label
• Set unit to 'milliseconds' or 'seconds'

spec.title: bytes_rate — Log Ingestion Volume per Service
spec.description:
Measures how many bytes of log data are ingested per second, per service.

🔧 Customize:
• bytes_rate() counts raw bytes of log lines (no parsing needed)
• Change 'namespace' label and value to match your environment
• group by a different label: by(cluster), by(pod), etc.
• Set unit to 'Bps' (bytes per second)
• Useful for estimating log ingestion cost per service

spec.title: unwrap — Min / Avg / Max of Numeric Field
spec.description:
Aggregate a numeric field extracted from logs into a table showing min, avg, max, and total per service.

🔧 Customize:
• Each query (A–D) uses a different aggregation: min, avg, max, sum
• Match the parsing stage (json/logfmt) and field name to your logs
• Change 'app' in by() to group by a different dimension
• Switch panel type to 'table' and use 'Last' reducer for a stat summary
• Great for request size, response time, or queue depth analysis

spec.title: LogQL Query Templates
